history.summary: A distinct early-20th-century shrine near the Mahakaleshwar Temple at Vikram Marg, Sethi Nagar, Ujjain - NOT a duplicate of the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga (seq 559), which is a Shiva temple, nor of the ancient Chintaman Ganesh Temple (seq 562), which stands ~6-7 km away on the Fatehabad road. The large Ganesha idol was established in 1904 (per astrologer Pandit Anandshankar Vyas; his grandfather Narayanji Vyas is credited with building the big idol, and a Tripadvisor account attributes the temple to freedom fighter Pandit Surya Narayan Vyas - verify). The complex's Panchmukhi Hanuman idol, in ashtadhatu and about 150 years old, predates the Ganesh idol; a larger Hanuman idol was added so devotees could have convenient darshan. Online sources describe the big Ganesh idol as made of masala, lentils, jaggery and herbs (verify). Temple Yatri alternatively links the shrine to a Vikramaditya legend or Ahilyabai Holkar - unconfirmed. CSV town/state (Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh) are correct; coordinates are street-level approximate for Vikram Marg, Sethi Nagar (verify).

name: Bade Ganeshji Ka Mandir
town_description: Ancient city on the Shipra (Kshipra) River in Madhya Pradesh, one of Hinduism's seven Sapta Puri, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and the Simhastha Kumbh Mela held every 12 years.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore (~55 km)
travel.railway: Ujjain Junction, connected to all major stations of India
travel.road: Well connected by road; regular buses from Indore, Bhopal and other MP cities

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Ganesh Chaturthi draws large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00 PM-8:00 PM vs 5:00 AM-7:00 PM (verify)
